title: Affine continuity for coordinate-supported geometric stalks
statement:
Fix the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A$ of [def-pur-conventions], with $n\geq1$, an integer $r$, and $b\geq0$. Let $R$ be any commutative $k$-algebra and let $I$ be the small directed poset of its finitely generated $k$-subalgebras, ordered by inclusion. Put $B_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $P_i=\mathbf A^b_{B_i}$, $P=\mathbf A^b_B$, and let $C_i\subseteq P_i$, $C\subseteq P$ be the zero sections [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-affine-space]. The projections $u_i:P\to P_i$ form the inverse limit of these schemes. Let $j_i:P_i\setminus C_i\hookrightarrow P_i$ and $j:P\setminus C\hookrightarrow P$ be the complementary opens [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the ordinary small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the finite twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the kernel support functors $Q_i,Q$ of [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support] with bounded-below right derived functors [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For every geometric point $\bar x$ on $C$, let $\bar x_i=u_i\bar x$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For every integer $d$, the canonical supported pullback legs induce an $A$-linear isomorphism
$$\varinjlim_i\mathcal H^d(RQ_i(A_{P_i}(r)))_{\bar x_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^d(RQ(A_P(r)))_{\bar x}.$$
The transitions and legs are those obtained from the kernel inclusions and restriction units in the support localization triangles, equivalently from the degreewise higher-direct-image exchanges for $j_i,j$. Both negative-degree sides vanish. These isomorphisms commute with maps of the constant coefficient lines $L_r=A(r)(k)$, their tensor and dual identifications, the supported pullback of ordered coordinate Kummer products from $\mathbf A^b_k$, and the corresponding localization boundary maps. They are unchanged on passing to any cofinal directed family of finitely generated subalgebras with union $R$, and are compatible with localizing $R$ at one element, using stages containing that element. Thus constructions at a geometric point from two affine base neighbourhoods agree on a common affine refinement when the finite-stage coordinate orientations agree under base change. For $b=0$, the punctured opens are empty and the same assertions hold.

source.place: Tag 0EYM (lemma-relative-colimit-general) for punctured-open higher-image continuity; Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support) for the kernel/cokernel support calculation. Agent extraction of coordinate-model Steps 3--4 and cofinal/affine refinements in Step 7; the supported-stalk consequence is to be proved, not quoted from the tag.

proof.text: Write $U_i=P_i\setminus C_i$. In the affine description of [def-sbc-affine-space], $U_i=\bigcup_{h=1}^bD(t_h)$ and $D(t_h)=\operatorname{Spec}R_i[t_1,\ldots,t_b,t_h^{-1}]$. Thus $j_i$ is quasi-compact; it is separated since it is an open immersion, whose diagonal is an isomorphism. Transition maps of the $P_i$ are affine, and $U_j=P_j\times_{P_i}U_i$, so those of the $U_i$ are affine too: on each displayed principal open they are induced by ring maps. Also $U=\varprojlim U_i$: fix the least stage $R_0=k$ (if $R=0$, there is no geometric point and the assertion is vacuous); a cone to the $U_i=P_i\times_{P_0}U_0$ is exactly a cone to the $P_i$ together with its compatible factorization to $U_0$. The given limit property of $P$ identifies this with a map to $P\times_{P_0}U_0=U$. Hence the punctured-open system has precisely the hypotheses of relative higher-image continuity. The same reasoning applies after restricting to a cofinal family, by extending a cone uniquely along that family.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general: verification of its geometric hypotheses for the coordinate opens

proof.text: Put $F_i=A_{P_i}(r)$ and $F=A_P(r)$, using the finite etale twists. They are the constant line sheaves with fibre $L_r=A(r)(k)$, with their canonical pullback identifications. This interpretation involves finite twists only: take $N=\ell^M$ annihilating $A$. Over $k$, $x^N-1$ has all its distinct roots, so the roots sheaf on every $k$-scheme is the constant finite sheaf $\mu_N(k)$ (the factors $x-\zeta$ are pairwise comaximal since $\zeta-\zeta'$ is a nonzero element of $k$). Tensor with $A$, then take tensor powers or the rank-one dual for negative $r$, as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The finite reduction identification in [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] identifies this with the finite twists specified in the item. Consequently every transition $u_{ji}^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ is the identity of this pulled-back line, and $\varinjlim_i (u_i|_U)^{-1}(F_i|_{U_i})=F|_U$. Indeed the diagram after pullback is the constant diagram on $F|_U$ with identity arrows over a nonempty directed index.

source.place: Tag 03PK, section-kummer, finite root sheaves; the finite reductions of the twists in the item

proof.text: For any of these pairs $(P_i,C_i)$, the module sheaves on $P_{i,\mathrm{et}}$ have enough injectives: by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] a sheaf $M$ has a degreewise-injective resolution $M\to I$, and $M\cong Z^0(I)\subseteq I^0$. So [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence] gives a resolution $F_i\to I_i$ by injective modules in degrees $\ge0$, and $I_i$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. Hence [lem-pur-etale-injective-support-sequence] applies to $I_i$ and computes the support triangle: its first complex is exactly $Q_i(I_i)$, by [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support], and its last is $j_{i,*}j_i^*I_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] (2), $Q_i(I_i)$ computes $RQ_iF_i$; it vanishes in negative degrees, so both negative-degree sides are zero. Thus for $K_i^d=\mathcal H^d(RQ_iF_i)$ the long exact sequence gives $0\to K_i^0\to F_i\to j_{i,*}(F_i|_{U_i})\to K_i^1\to0$ and, for $d\ge2$, $K_i^d\cong R^{d-1}j_{i,*}(F_i|_{U_i})$ through the connecting map. The same holds on $P$ for $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0A45, lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle, kernel/cokernel and shifted higher-image calculation; module version via Tag 093X

proof.text: These exact sequences form compatible diagrams under the supported pullbacks in the question, including their connecting arrows. Here is the comparison on resolutions. For a transition or limit leg $v:P'\to P_i$, exact module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives a quasi-isomorphism $v^*F_i\to v^*I_i$. Choose, as in step 3, a bounded-below injective (hence K-injective) resolution $I'$ of $F'$, and use [lem-sp-kinjective-comparison-principle] to lift $v^*F_i\to F'\to I'$ to $v^*I_i\to I'$, uniquely up to homotopy. The ordinary open exchange $v^*j_{i,*}j_i^*I_i\to j'_*j'^*v^*I_i$, followed by this lift, and the middle lift carry the restriction unit to the restriction unit. Exactness of $v^*$ therefore gives the induced map on the kernels. These three maps give a morphism of the short exact support complexes of step 3. Their right-hand map is the usual derived open exchange, and their left-hand map derives the kernel factorization specified in the item. Applying the same construction to a homotopy gives a homotopy on kernels, so compositions and identities hold on the derived objects; the connecting maps commute by the short-exact-complex construction (a cycle is lifted to the middle complex and its differential taken in the kernel). This fixes the maps, rather than choosing an unspecified completion of a triangle.

source.place: Tag 093X, lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective; lemma-base-change-map-flat-case, construction on resolutions; explicit kernel comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-0eym] to $j_i:U_i\to P_i$ and the underlying abelian sheaves of $F_i|_{U_i}$, with step 1 giving affine transitions and qcqs $j_i$, and step 2 giving the limiting sheaf. To identify this with the module comparison use [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]: all transition and limit squares here are cartesian, and its clauses (1)--(3) identify inverse images, derived direct images and their actual exchange maps after forgetting scalars. Every map is $A$-linear before forgetting. Apply [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits] and [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] to obtain, for every $q\ge0$, the $A$-linear isomorphism $\varinjlim_i(R^qj_{i,*}F_i|_{U_i})_{\bar x_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}(R^qj_*F|_U)_{\bar x}$. The central term comparison $\varinjlim_i(F_i)_{\bar x_i}\to F_{\bar x}$ is the identity on $L_r$. These are the legs of the exact-sequence diagram of step 4, not arbitrary isomorphisms between its terms.

source.place: Tag 0EYM, lemma-relative-colimit-general, statement and specified comparison; Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback

proof.text: Take geometric stalks of the sequences in step 3, using [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and then filtered colimits using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. Thus $\varinjlim_iK^0_{i,\bar x_i}$ is the kernel and $\varinjlim_iK^1_{i,\bar x_i}$ the cokernel of the colimit arrow $L_r\to\varinjlim_i(j_{i,*}F_i|_{U_i})_{\bar x_i}$. The commutative square of step 5 identifies this arrow with $F_{\bar x}\to(j_*F|_U)_{\bar x}$, with both vertical arrows invertible. Restricting those invertible arrows to kernels and taking their quotients therefore proves the required comparisons in degrees $0,1$. In degree $d\ge2$, use the isomorphism of step 3 with $q=d-1$ and step 5. Step 4 identifies each resulting map with the supported leg and guarantees compatibility with the localization boundaries. Negative degrees were settled in step 3.

source.place: Tag 0A45, lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle, applied to the Tag 0EYM comparison on stalks

proof.text: The entire argument is natural in a map of the constant coefficient lines: on resolutions use the same lift construction as step 4; on kernels, cokernels and the exchanges it is just the induced map. To check the claimed tensor/dual identifications, choose an $A$-basis of each rank-one line $L_r$ over $k$. A map is then multiplication by an element of $A$, and tensor multiplication or evaluation of duals is $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. The maps of steps 4--6 are $A$-linear, so inserting these identifications on the coefficient factor commutes with them; changing basis multiplies both paths by the same unit. This asserts compatibility with the coefficient-line identifications, without asserting that tensor products of two supported complexes themselves satisfy a new continuity theorem. For coordinate Kummer products use [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality]: $\kappa(t_h)$ pulls back to $\kappa(t_h)$, its individual support boundary pulls back to that boundary, and the ordered supported product pulls back to that same ordered product. On every pointed etale neighbourhood the global-to-supported-stalk map factors the usual germ through the support kernel, by [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support]. Thus a class from $\mathbf A^b_k$ has at each stage and at the limit exactly its canonical supported germ; step 4 and hence the comparison of step 6 carry those germs to one another. No finite-stage orientation theorem or purity is used.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, functorial restrictions and boundaries; blueprint coordinate-model normalization clause

proof.text: For a cofinal directed family, a class or an equality in the filtered colimit can be represented at a stage by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise]; choose a member of the family above that stage. This proves both surjectivity and injectivity of the reindexing map. Its composite with the comparison of step 6 is the old leg on each representative, so the isomorphism is unchanged. For $f\in R$, first take the cofinal stages containing $f$. The rings $R_i[1/f]$ are finitely generated $k$-algebras with union $R[1/f]$ (a finite list of numerators and $f$ lies in one stage). The corresponding coordinate squares and their punctured opens are cartesian; step 4 gives the commuting ladders for $R_i\to R_i[1/f]$ and $R\to R[1/f]$. Taking their colimits gives the asserted localization compatibility. At a point in two affine base neighbourhoods, choose an affine neighbourhood inside their intersection and then principal affine neighbourhoods of that point inside it and each original affine: principal opens form a basis in an affine spectrum. Apply the localization comparison to these restrictions. If finite-stage orientations agree under base change, their images are equal there by these commuting ladders. This proves the stated agreement on a common affine refinement; it does not require the whole intersection of affine opens to be affine.

source.place: Tag 0EYM: cofinal reindexing and explicit affine-local compatibility of the same canonical legs

proof.text: If $b=0$, $C_i=P_i$ and $U_i=\varnothing$, so $j_{i,*}j_i^*=0$ and $Q_i=\mathrm{id}$, directly from the defining kernel. Likewise $Q=\mathrm{id}$. The asserted colimit is the identity $L_r\to L_r$ in degree zero and $0\to0$ otherwise; all boundaries to/from the empty open are zero and the coordinate product is the empty product $1$. Thus all compatibility assertions persist, including negative degrees. For any zero ring base or empty affine refinement there is no geometric point to check.
